Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Rules The rules ( https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djambi ) leave space for interpretation on some fine points of the game. Choices made for the BGA implementation are the following: - you can kill your own pieces , except the leader (sometimes sacrifice is necessary); - the Reporter has the choice not to kill (the Press is not above making some arrangements with political parties); - a Chief is eliminated if fully entrapped by corpses with no Necromobile left in play; - the master move of the Diplomat is available (removing a Chief from the Maze, then replacing them by another Chief when leaving the Maze); - the master move of the Assassin is available (killing a Chief in power, then killing another Chief when leaving the Maze and setting up their corpse in the Maze as a puppet regime!) - when only two players are left, if chief A enters the maze, the next turn will be for player B , before player A gets two consecutive turns. Credits Illustrations for the "Whimsy" theme (see game preferences) have been created by Reno ( http://reno-pixellu.com/blog/ ), Boulet ( http://www.bouletcorp.com ) and Lucie Albon ( http://www.luciealbon.net/ ). [Rating: 3/10] I think abstracts should be played with 2 players. I don't like politics in most games and this is definitely one of it.

[Rating: 3/10] Maybe this would be a better game if all players were at the same skill level.  Unfortunately, the game balance is very fragile, giving HUGE advantages to the players that play after the weak players.

[Rating: 5/10] An alright abstract war game.  I like that when you take over an enemy their pieces become part of your army.  I dislike that you only get one turn though as the first person to get a person to submit will then be targeted 2-1 and it's then very unlikely that they'll win.
